title: Triage a production bug: which panel first?
purpose: Choose the first DevTools panel from the symptom a user reports, and see what evidence each panel gives.
summary: A user reports a problem on a live site. The deck groups six symptoms: a slow first load, slow clicks, growing memory, a broken layout, old data after a deploy and an error only on an iPhone. Each branch opens the panel that records the matching evidence, shows what to read there, and names the cost of opening the wrong panel first.
explanation: Each panel records one kind of evidence, so the symptom tells you which panel can show the cause first.

learning_check.question: A page gets slower each time a user opens and closes a dialog. Which panel do you open first, and what do you do there?
learning_check.answer: Memory: take a heap snapshot, open and close the dialog, take a second snapshot, and compare them to see what grows.

slides.heading: A user reports a bug. Where do you look?
slides.notes: State the decision: DevTools has many panels, and the first one you open decides how fast you find evidence.

visual.subtitle: Start from the symptom, not from your favorite panel

slides.heading: Each panel records one kind of evidence
slides.notes: Name what each panel records. The symptom tells you which kind of evidence holds the cause.

items: Network: every request and its timing phases
Performance: main-thread tasks on a timeline
Memory: what the JavaScript heap holds
Elements: the DOM and the CSS rules that apply
Application: service workers, caches and storage

slides.heading: Symptoms of speed and memory
slides.notes: Three symptoms look alike to a user: the site feels slow. Open each branch to see which panel separates them.

items: The tab gets slower the longer it is open

slides.heading: Symptoms of a wrong result
slides.notes: These three symptoms show wrong output, not slow output. Open each branch to see where the cause is recorded.

items: Users see old data after a deploy
An error happens only on an iPhone

slides.heading: The triage rule
slides.notes: Turn the branches into one repeatable procedure that works for a symptom you have not seen before.

items: Write the symptom in one sentence
Open the panel that records that evidence
Reproduce the problem while it records
Change code only after the evidence names a cause

slides.heading: Open Network and read the Timing tab
slides.notes: Tick Disable cache to load the page like a first-time visitor, pick a slow throttling preset, reload, then open the slowest request's Timing tab.

items: Tick Disable cache: you load like a first-time visitor
Open the slowest request, then its Timing tab
Long Waiting (TTFB): look at the server
Long Content Download: look at file size

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: Memory
slides.notes: A heap snapshot shows what JavaScript holds in memory. It has no request timing, so it cannot show a slow server or a large file.

left.label: Network first
items: Points to server or file size

visual.verdict: A slow load is a request problem until the Timing tab says otherwise.

slides.heading: Open Performance and record the click
slides.notes: Click Record, repeat the slow click, stop. In the Main track a task over 50 ms is a long task; the part beyond 50 ms is red. Bottom-up shows which function used the time.

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: Network
slides.notes: Network lists requests. A click handler that only runs JavaScript sends no request, so Network shows nothing slow while the main thread is busy.

right.label: Network first
items: You may blame a fast request

visual.verdict: Slow input is a main-thread problem until the trace says otherwise.

slides.heading: Name the memory symptom first
slides.notes: The memory docs list three symptoms. Progressive slowdown suggests a leak, constant bad performance suggests bloat, and frequent pauses suggest frequent garbage collection.

slides.heading: Compare two heap snapshots
slides.notes: Take a heap snapshot, do the action and undo it, take a second snapshot, then use the Comparison view. Detached DOM nodes are removed from the page but still referenced by JavaScript.

events.label: Comparison view
events.detail: what grew, such as detached DOM nodes

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: one snapshot
slides.notes: One snapshot shows the heap at one moment. A leak is growth, so you need two snapshots around the same action to see it.

visual.verdict: A leak is a change over time, so measure twice.

slides.heading: Open Elements and inspect the box
slides.notes: Right-click the broken element and choose Inspect. The Styles pane lists the CSS rules that apply, shows overridden ones crossed out, and lets you edit a value to test a fix live.

items: Right-click the broken element, choose Inspect
Read the Styles pane: which rules apply
Edit a value live to test the fix

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: Sources
slides.notes: Sources pauses JavaScript. When a CSS rule causes the broken layout, stepping through scripts spends time on code that is not the cause.

visual.verdict: Inspect the box before you debug the script.

slides.heading: Open Application, then Network
slides.notes: In Application, the Service Workers tab shows the active worker and offers Update on reload and Bypass for network. Cache Storage lists cached responses. In Network, tick Disable cache and reload to compare.

items: Application, Service Workers: which worker is active
Tick Update on reload or Bypass for network
Application, Cache Storage: the cached responses
Network, Disable cache: reload and compare

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: Elements
slides.notes: Elements shows the old value in the DOM. It does not show where the value came from, a cache, a service worker or the server.

visual.verdict: Find where the data came from, not only what it shows.

slides.heading: Attach Web Inspector to the real iPhone
slides.notes: On the iPhone, turn on Safari, Advanced, Web Inspector. On the Mac, turn on the Safari developer features, connect the cable, then pick the device in the Develop menu and read its Console and Sources.

items: iPhone: Settings, Safari, Advanced, Web Inspector on
Mac Safari: show features for web developers
Develop menu: pick the iPhone and the page
Read the error in the device's Console

slides.heading: Wrong first choice: device mode only
slides.notes: Chrome device mode is a first-order approximation: the page still runs in desktop Chrome on your laptop. An error that comes from the phone's browser may not appear there.

left.label: Real device
items: Needs a cable and a Mac

visual.verdict: Use device mode for layout; use the real device for a device-only error.
